correctness.rationale: PASS: For synchronous Greenberg-Hastings 0/1/2 rule on K_{a,b,c}, a rainbow transversal triangle (all three colors across parts) rotates and cannot lose excitation. Conversely, with all three colors globally present but no transversal rainbow, Hall SDR theorem forces two parts to have union size one, hence both monochromatic in the same state j; unique remaining part contains both other states. A direct update table shows extinction at t=2,3,4 when j=2,1,0 respectively, including the possibility j is also in exceptional part. For globally at most two states, time-1 {0,2}, time-2 {1,2}, time-3 generally {0,1}, and time-4 {0,1} with all excited vertices confined to one mixed part. For a part of size k the number of exceptional assignments containing both other colors is q_k=3^k−2^{k+1}+1, giving Q=sum q. Therefore d0=1, d1=2^N−1, d2=2^N−1+Q, d3=2^N+4−S+Q, d4=S−6+Q, dt>=5=0; sum E=3*2^N−3+3Q. Sharp cutoff 3 only at (1,1,1), otherwise 4. Independent direct vertex-state simulation verified all 10 triples with 1<=a<=b<=c<=3 (32670 labelled configurations).
